narrative_purpose: Show the pivotal distinction visually: a survivable burn (secondary succession, soil and roots intact) versus a sterilising burial (primary succession, only bare rock), side by side.
subject: A split-frame comparison. LEFT HALF: a fire-blackened forest floor where bright green shoots resprout from surviving charred tree stumps, the dark soil beneath intact and threaded with roots. RIGHT HALF: a deep grey pyroclastic burial, a calcined bare tree skeleton, only sterile mineral rock and ash with nothing growing and no visible soil.
scene: Two adjacent Pandoran aftermaths divided by a clear vertical seam down the middle of the frame; left side charred but living, right side buried and dead.
camera: Straight-on mid shot, both halves at the same eye level so the contrast reads immediately.
light: Left half carries faint living cyan-green glow from the resprouting shoots; right half is flat, cold, unglowing grey-indigo.
palette: Left: charred black with living teal-green accents. Right: uniform stone-grey and void indigo, no life colour.
style: Painterly naturalist comparison plate, the two halves clearly distinct in mood.
detail_level: Even detail on both halves so the resprouting shoots and the sterile rock are equally legible.
composition: Clean vertical split down the centre, matched framing on each side, a charred stump on the left mirrored by a bare skeleton on the right.
consistency_notes: Left = secondary succession (soil and roots survive, green returns); right = primary succession (sterile rock, nothing left). The seam between them is the whole point. Cool Pandora palette; green only on the living left half.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no 3D-render or photographic look, no cartoon style, no neon glow
